gen-gf-happy-monkey-manrope: Happy Monkey draws bold, ruler-straight lines with wide gaps in its e. Manrope, the sans-serif below, leaves a bright open gap at every curve and stands taller in the lowercase than the heading.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-montserrat: Loud meets wiry: Happy Monkey holds a ruler-straight line with wide gaps in the e. And Montserrat, the plain sans, glides under it on a taller lowercase, with generous white space before every curve.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-satoshi: Distinctive, Happy Monkey draws ruler-straight lines with wide gaps in its e. Satoshi, with its soaring x-height and open e, lets a whole page of text flow along without any tightness.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-switzer: Switzer brings Swiss tidiness, with wire-like letterforms and c tips that never creep toward touching. But Happy Monkey, bold and ruler-straight, has a moderate lowercase against the taller sans, and that gap is the draw.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-work-sans: Happy Monkey is all bold, distinctive swagger, with ruler-straight lines and wide gaps in the e. Work Sans does the opposite job, staying contemporary, with c tips that never creep toward touching.
gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-fs-bespoke-: Stubby and sure of itself: Love Ya Like A Sister keeps ascenders barely clearing the x-height. And Bespoke Sans offers a sharp, refined counterpoint, with generous space between curve ends and the stem.
gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-gf-abeezee: ABeeZee is approachable, with terminals that finish well away from the stem and strokes like neon glass tubing. Love Ya Like A Sister gives it a bold, level, expressive partner.
gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-gf-aldrich: Cupped rounds and a thick single thread: Aldrich, a modern sans, runs close to cap height under Love Ya Like A Sister. That heading earns its keep big and short.
gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-gf-alexandr: Alexandria is a clean, professional sans-serif, tall in the body with short stems and generously opened c terminals. Love Ya Like A Sister brings bold, stencil-flat lines on top.
gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-gf-amiko: Amiko reads modern and neutral, a sans with outward-pointing terminals like tongs and a crayon-bold lowercase. Love Ya Like A Sister, drawn with one fixed nib, brings the volume.
